newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-BOLIVIA HIT BY INJURY CRISIS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BOLIVIA HIT BY INJURY CRISIS.

text.p: Bolivia have been hit by an injury crisis in the run-up to next week's World Cup qualifier at home to Argentina.
Striker Juan Berthy Suarez, leading scoring in the Bolivian championship, became the latest player to withdraw from the match through injury, team doctor Miguel Elias said on Thursday.

Bolivia coach Antonio Lopes has already been deprived of striker Erwin Sanchez and midfielder Julio Balidivieso, while goalkeeper Carlos Trucco, midfielder Sergio Castillo and striker Richard Cueto are all doubtful.
To add to Bolivia's woes, midfield playmaker Marco Etcheverry is suspended after receiving two yellow cards.

Bolivia are sixth in the nine-team group, which is halfway through its marathon qualification competition. Bottom-placed Venezuela are the only country who have no realistic chance of taking one of the four qualifying places.
However, the Bolivians, who are poor travellers, have played six of their eight games to date at home, where the altitude of the capital La Paz gives them a huge advantage.

Their preparations suffered a further blow on Sunday when a warm-up game at home to Jamaica turned into a farce. The Jamaicans, unable to cope with the thin air in the mining town of Oruro, gave up and began clowning around on the pitch during their 6-0 defeat.
Argentina, third in the group, revived their hopes by beating group leaders Colombia 1-0 away in February.
For the last three weeks they have been acclimatising in the town of La Quiaca, high in the bleak Altiplano on the border with Bolivia.
